II-A, Alg. 2: after optimisation the agent keeps checking the new trajectory against received trajectories for a window delta_DC; if a potential collision is found the new trajectory is discarded and the agent keeps executing its committed trajectory; Prop. 1 guarantees collision-free operation when delta_max <= delta_DC.
method: Decentralised asynchronous planner with delay check, two-step trajectory publication and trajectory storing/checking that vetoes commitment of newly optimised trajectories under bounded communication delay.
evaluation: 10-agent simulation, 100 runs per delay (0-300 ms) vs EGO-Swarm, EDG-Team, MADER and no-Check ablation: 100% collision-free vs 70-95% MADER; travel time/stops; 22 flights with 2-6 UAVs on Intel NUC10 onboard.
contribution: Robust MADER adds a delay-check veto and two-step trajectory commitment so decentralised asynchronous UAV planners remain provably collision-free under bounded communication delay, validated in simulation and 2-6 UAV flights.
flag: Interceptor vetoes commitment of a new plan rather than halting execution. Delay bound violated ~25% of the time on hardware without collision (Sec. IV-A). Trade-off: more stops and longer travel time (relevant to RQ5). (d) borderline: explicit comm-delay window but no inference-latency constraint.

title: SRL-ORCA: A Socially Aware Multi-Agent Mapless Navigation Algorithm in Complex Dynamic Scenes
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
evidence: Sec. IV-B(2): the RL velocity is executed if inside the priority-ORCA set, otherwise replaced by the closest feasible velocity (Eq. 17) or by an ORCA 3D linear program when the set is empty (Eq. 18).
method: PPO policy with curiosity for decentralised mapless multi-robot navigation; ORCA acts as an execution-time shield that keeps, corrects or replaces each RL velocity; social-norm reward penalties.
evaluation: Gazebo/Unity, 2 and 8 robots, 4 scenarios; baselines NH-ORCA, DRL, Hybrid-RL; success, collision (robot/obstacle), social-rule success, time-to-target; 6 Turtlebot3 demo; no per-step latency.
contribution: Shields a learned multi-robot navigation policy with ORCA at execution time, replacing unsafe velocities while learning social traffic norms; collision and success rates compared with DRL and ORCA baselines.
flag: Borderline on primacy: paper is framed as navigation/social-norm learning, shield is off-the-shelf ORCA; residual 2.7% robot collisions attributed to compute limits; no latency numbers; real-robot results not quantified.

title: Safe Multiagent Motion Planning Under Uncertainty for Drones Using Filtered Reinforcement Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
evidence: Sec. III-B: the safety filter takes the RL control sequence and computes safe control inputs that minimally deviate from it; only the first safe control is applied and the problem is re-solved each step.
method: Single-agent RL reference planner wrapped by a centralised convex QP safety filter with risk-tightened chance constraints (obstacles, inter-agent, keep-in) and viability-set terminal constraints for recursive feasibility.
evaluation: 100 Monte Carlo sims: 99% success vs 92% (no terminal constraint) vs 55% pure MPC; min separations; 2-24 agent scaling; 6 Crazyflies, QP 0.05 s mean (max 0.06 s) within 0.1 s period on workstation.
contribution: Wraps a single-agent RL planner in a convex chance-constrained safety filter that overrides unsafe commands for multiple drones, with recursive feasibility and real-time solve times demonstrated on hardware.
flag: (d) is partial: solve time is reported against a 0.1 s control period but no explicit deadline constraint or edge deployment; filter is centralised; collision rate reported only via success/min-separation.

title: Safety-Critical Control with Uncertainty Quantification using Adaptive Conformal Prediction
venue: 2024 American Control Conference (ACC)
evidence: Sec. III-C: the ACP-quantified CBF constraint is embedded in the MPC optimisation (Eq. 9b); Sec. IV-B/C report that all CBF-baseline paths collide while ACP-SBC paths remain collision-free for 30 single-integrator and 6 unicycle robots.
method: Adaptive conformal prediction estimates CBF prediction-error quantiles online under unknown noise; tightened probabilistic CBF constraints are embedded in MPC for multi-robot collision avoidance.
evaluation: Simulation only (single integrator, CoppeliaSim Khepera unicycles); 3 noise distributions, 30 robots, 20 seeds; baseline CBF only; metric minimum inter-robot/obstacle distance (plots, no tabulated rates); no compute time.
contribution: Combines adaptive conformal prediction with probabilistic control barrier functions inside MPC to give distribution-free high-probability collision avoidance for multi-robot teams under unknown motion noise.
flag: Thin evaluation: single CBF baseline, no numerical collision/violation rates, no ablation of ACP; constraint is inside the planner so (a) is NOT met; maintainer may judge E2.

title: Stackelberg Game-Theoretic Trajectory Guidance for Multi-Robot Systems with Koopman Operator
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. VI: 'There are remaining challenges to ensure safety when employing the Koopman operator for mission-critical applications'; obstacle constraints are inside the leader's receding-horizon OCP (Sec. IV-B); no collision metric reported.
method: Leader-follower Stackelberg game; leader learns a Koopman linear model of the follower's feedback behaviour and uses it in receding-horizon planning for trajectory guidance.
evaluation: Simulation only, 2 unicycle robots, 4 obstacles; baselines model-based OCP, one-step NN, DMD; metrics prediction error, planning time (about halved), control cost; no collision or safety metric; RTX 6000 for training.
contribution: Learns a Koopman operator model of a follower robot's responses so a leader can plan collision-free guidance trajectories faster than model-based Stackelberg planning in simulation.
flag: Only two robots; primary claims are prediction accuracy and planning speed; Koopman model is latent prediction of another agent (nominal (b)) but no safety metric at all, so E2 would also apply.

title: ZAPP! Zonotope Agreement of Prediction and Planning for Continuous-Time Collision Avoidance with Discrete-Time Dynamics
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Abstract/Sec. V: numerical examples 'show how ZAPP can produce safer trajectories compared to baselines in interactive scenes'; Table I: ZAPP 3.3% crashes vs MATS 30.0% in a hallway with 10 interactive agents.
method: Zonotope reachable-set prediction (Trajectron++) at coarse time steps converted to continuous-time collision-avoidance constraints in gradient-based MPC; sub-differentiable zonotope collision check with interaction gradients.
evaluation: Simulated hallway, 10 social-force agents, ~30 runs/method; baselines MATS, MATS w/o DC, ZAPP w/o DC, ZAPP w/o interaction gradients; goal/crash %, speed, solve time 4.33 s (not real time); no hardware.
contribution: Reconciles coarse multi-agent trajectory prediction with fine-grained planning by representing predictions as zonotopes, cutting crash rate from 30% to 3.3% against a discrete-time baseline in interactive simulations.
flag: Single controlled ego agent among predicted agents; safety enforced as planner constraints (no runtime shield); solve time an order of magnitude slower than real time; simulation only.

title: Addressing Non-Intervention Challenges via Resilient Robotics Utilizing a Digital Twin
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Omni-layer Intelligent Systems (COINS)
evidence: Sec. III: 'the information is fed to a human-in-the-loop operator to draw on their expertise'; Sec. IV: the work 'represents a proof of concept' with two runs and no quantitative results.
method: Bidirectional Unity digital twin (ODSI) with TCP client-server links to a heterogeneous robot fleet; operator triggers missions; simulated battery fault triggers pre-determined recovery by another robot.
evaluation: Lab-scale offshore analogue, Husky+UR5s, Tello, Spot; two runs (nominal and induced fault); no baselines, no metrics (no failure rate, recovery time, interventions, trials); no latency measurements.
contribution: Demonstrates a bidirectional digital twin through which a human operator and a heterogeneous robot fleet jointly recover from a simulated robot failure without on-site intervention.
flag: Qualitative proof of concept only; decision logic and safety-stop block described but not implemented or tested; handoff protocol undefined.

title: Communication-Critical Planning via Multi-Agent Trajectory Exchange
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Abstract: vehicles 'must navigate through a busy intersection while avoiding collisions with each other and with obstacles'; Table II: top-1 hard collision rate falls from 18.3% (1 agent) to 7.9% (8 agents), a 57% reduction.
method: Learned BEV semantic occupancy forecasting per agent; ego broadcasts candidate trajectories, peers return sampled cost and entropy values which are fused to rank and select the lowest-cost trajectory.
evaluation: InD real tracks, AutoCastSim (CARLA), authors' CoBEV-Sim with up to 20 agents; baselines single-agent and random sampler; metrics hard collision rate, pixel accuracy 72.5%, mIoU; bandwidth estimated analytically; no hardware or latency.
contribution: Reduces hard collision rate by up to 57% at busy intersections by letting connected vehicles exchange candidate trajectories and return uncertainty-weighted costs from their own occupancy forecasts.
flag: Collision avoidance is a cost in trajectory ranking, not a runtime veto; baselines limited to single-agent/random; bandwidth claim unmeasured; 'hard collision' not precisely defined.

title: Constructive Barrier Feedback for Collision Avoidance in Leader-Follower Formation Control
venue: 2023 62nd IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
evidence: Sec. III: control law u_i = u_i^n - k_o g_i f^B(d_i_dot, d_i) adds 'a dissipative control barrier feedback slowing down the relative velocity in the direction of the neighbor', using 'explicit control barrier feedback instead of relying on quadratic programming barrier constraints'; Sec. IV: without the term 'agents collide with their neighbor'.
method: Additive divergent-flow damping term in leader-follower formation controller for 3D double-integrator agents on a chain topology; Lyapunov-style proof that neighbor distance margin stays positive.
evaluation: Simulation only, 4 agents, static formation; ablation with vs without barrier term (k_o=0); qualitative plots of distance margin and errors; no collision statistics, trials, hardware or timing.
contribution: Adds a constructive divergent-flow barrier feedback to leader-follower formation control so neighboring agents provably avoid collision without solving a barrier QP.
flag: Collision avoidance is primary claim and term is ablated, but outcome is a single qualitative 4-agent plot with no quantitative safety metric; term is baked into control law, not a runtime filter. Computational-efficiency claim is unmeasured.

title: Data-Driven Risk-sensitive Model Predictive Control for Safe Navigation in Multi-Robot Systems
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. II-A/III-A: collision avoidance is enforced via a distributionally robust CVaR constraint on robot-obstacle distance inside the finite-horizon MPC; Sec. IV: collision percentage and average minimum inter-agent distance are compared against deterministic MPC in distributed and decentralized settings over 50 runs.
method: Per-robot receding-horizon MPC with Wasserstein distributionally robust CVaR collision constraint over empirical prediction-error samples; convex/minimax duality gives tractable finite-dimensional reformulation; distributed and decentralized variants.
evaluation: 2-agent numerical crossing (50 runs; alpha, theta, noise swept) vs deterministic MPC: collision % and min distance; 6-drone Gazebo demo qualitative only; Ryzen 5800H, IPOPT solve 41+/-12 ms at T=20, Ns=10 (up to 184 ms).
contribution: Distributionally robust CVaR collision constraints inside multi-robot MPC lower collision rates relative to deterministic MPC under prediction uncertainty in distributed and decentralized settings.
flag: Safety is a constraint inside the planner, not an interceptor (runtime_interceptor=no); quantitative collision results only in the 2-agent numerical study, Gazebo is qualitative. Solve times reported vs 0.1 s period but no explicit latency requirement, so (d) not credited.

title: Distributed Safety Verification for Multi-Agent Systems
venue: 2023 62nd IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
evidence: Sec. 3: centralized problem (7) minimizes sum ||u_i - u_i^des||^2 subject to sub-network CBF constraints, i.e. a QP safety filter on nominal inputs, solved by distributed primal decomposition (Alg. 1) with a truncated variant (Alg. 2); Sec. 4/Thm. 13: scenario-based verification bounds the probability of unsafety with confidence 1-beta.
method: Distributed CBF-QP safety filter via primal decomposition with relaxation variables (feasible local QPs), truncated-iteration variant, and distributed scenario-based verification yielding probabilistic unsafety bounds for any Lipschitz controller.
evaluation: Simulation: 10 heterogeneous double-integrator robots swapping positions; ablation eta=0 vs eta=30 iterations via summed constraint relaxation; 4-robot verification: violation prob in [0,0.146] at 90% confidence, empirical CDF over 300 repeats; no timing or hardware.
contribution: Distributes the multi-agent CBF-QP safety filter across agents with convergence guarantees, a truncated real-time-friendly variant, and distributed scenario-based bounds on the probability of unsafety.
flag: Meets evaluation floor only marginally: safety metric is residual constraint violation and probabilistic unsafety bound, no collision counts, no centralized-QP comparison, no timing despite real-time motivation of truncation.

title: Generalization of Safe Optimal Control Actions on Networked Multiagent Systems
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems
evidence: Sec. IV, Thm. 3/4: each component and composed optimal action is passed through a stochastic (higher-degree) CBF constrained minimum-deviation filter that finds 'the control closest to the nominal optimal action that satisfies the CBF constraint'; Sec. V-B Fig. 8: minimum obstacle distance vs CBF margin with and without the filter over 10 runs.
method: Compose safe optimal controllers for new tasks on networked multi-agent systems as weighted mixtures of component controllers, each filtered by stochastic higher-degree CBFs; composed action re-filtered; sample-free generalization.
evaluation: Matlab simulation: single UAV, 3-UAV and 5-UAV teams with obstacles; baseline = unfiltered optimal control; metric = minimum obstacle distance vs safety margin (10 runs); 5-UAV results qualitative; no timing or hardware.
contribution: Shows that stochastic CBF-filtered component controllers can be linearly composed to produce safe optimal actions for unseen tasks on networked UAV teams without resampling.
flag: Borderline: multi-agent only through cost coupling, safety is static-obstacle avoidance not inter-agent collision, composed controller is open-loop w.r.t. new state; quantitative safety evidence limited to min-distance plot with/without filter. RQ4 overlap is task composition, not hazard composition.

title: Learning Responsibility Allocations for Safe Human-Robot Interaction with Applications to Autonomous Driving
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. I: 'A primary use case of RA-CBFs is their application as a safety filter within an AV stack' revising nominal inputs when needed; Sec. V, Table I: closed-loop safety violation 0.833% (ours) vs 0.833% (Worst-Case) vs 2.50% (Even-Split) over 120 nuScenes scenarios.
method: Responsibility-Aware CBFs: pairwise multi-agent CBF with a learned scene-dependent responsibility allocation gamma (ResNet-18 + MLP) trained from human driving data with hinge loss and max-entropy regularizer; used as QP safety filter.
evaluation: nuScenes Boston Seaport, 120 closed-loop 10 s scenarios at 10 Hz with BITS traffic; baselines Worst-Case CBF and Even-Split; metrics: constraint violation, closed-loop safety violation, off-road time, distance covered; no hardware or latency reported.
contribution: Learns scene-dependent responsibility allocations from human driving data to build RA-CBF safety filters that match worst-case CBF safety while nearly matching the throughput of an even-split filter.
flag: Human element is human drivers as interaction partners and forensic culpability analysis, not takeover/handoff, so (e) not credited and human-handoff gap cell is weak; safety differences rest on 1-3 events out of 120.

title: MixNet: Physics Constrained Deep Neural Motion Prediction for Autonomous Racing
venue: IEEE Access
evidence: Sec. 4.5: inference for four vehicles takes 9 ms (MixNet) vs 15 ms (LSTM benchmark) against a stated 20 ms single-CPU-core budget; Sec. 3.3/3.4: multi-vehicle predictions are checked for mutual collisions and implausible outputs fall back to a rail-based prediction.
method: MixNet: LSTM encoder with decoder outputting softmax mixture weights over four track base curves plus piecewise accelerations, guaranteeing smooth in-track trajectories; multi-vehicle interaction collision check and rail-based fallback.
evaluation: HIL racing data (358k pairs, 10 test races); baseline LSTM encoder-decoder; metric MAE (4.91 vs 5.36 m) and robustness to noise; Intel i7-4720HQ single core, 9 ms inference for 4 vehicles under 20 ms budget; deployed at IAC 2021.
contribution: Physics-constrained mixture-of-base-curves motion predictor for multi-vehicle autonomous racing that beats an LSTM baseline in accuracy and runs in 9 ms on a single CPU core.
flag: Maintainer may override: strongest RQ1 latency evidence in batch (explicit 20 ms budget, 9 ms on single core, multi-agent prediction), but the only metric is prediction MAE, no safety metric; fallback overrides predictions not actions, so not an interceptor; (b) credited loosely (trajectory, not latent, prediction).

title: Multi-robot task allocation for safe planning against stochastic hazard dynamics
venue: 2023 European Control Conference (ECC)
evidence: Sec. II: safety is the probability of visiting targets and exiting without entering a hazardous cell, built into an offline stochastic-reachability policy and greedy task allocation; 'Collision avoidance among the robots is outside of the scope of our current study.'
method: Two-stage multi-robot mission planning: per-robot stochastic reachability DP against a spreading hazard, plus forward/reverse greedy auction-based target allocation maximizing product of per-robot safety probabilities with approximation bounds.
evaluation: Numerical: 3 robots, 5 targets on 17x13 grid vs brute-force optimum (0.699/0.717 vs 0.717 success probability); randomized study 2-5 robots, 2-7 targets, 20 instances each; Core i7 2.6 GHz, planning takes minutes (brute force ~5 h).
contribution: Scalable greedy task allocation with stochastic-reachability controllers for multi-robot missions under spreading hazards, with provable bounds on safety suboptimality.
flag: Planning-time allocation against an environmental hazard; no runtime interception, no inter-agent hazard (collisions explicitly out of scope), no handoff or latency aspect. Quantitative evaluation exists, so not E2.

title: Online Control Barrier Functions for Decentralized Multi-Agent Navigation
venue: 2023 International Symposium on Multi-Robot and Multi-Agent Systems (MRS)
evidence: Sec. III-B/IV: each agent solves a CLF-CBF QP per step whose CBF class-K parameters (zeta, eta) are set online by a PPO-trained GNN policy; the QP is itself the controller, no nominal action is filtered.
method: Online CBFs: GNN policy trained with PPO tunes per-agent CBF hyperparameters at runtime inside a decentralized CLF-CBF QP navigation controller.
evaluation: Sim with 4 agents (narrow passage, cross, singularity) vs grid-searched fixed CBFs and random time-varying CBFs; SPL and PCT-Speed over 20 seeds; 4 DJI RoboMasters (Raspberry Pi, ROS 2), qualitative. No timing.
contribution: Learns to tune control-barrier-function hyperparameters online with a graph neural network so decentralized multi-agent navigation stays feasible and fast where fixed CBFs stall.
flag: Borderline: CBF is a constraint inside the navigation QP, not a filter over a nominal action; paper is about feasibility/path quality (SPL, speed), collision rate not reported, so primacy test for (c) fails.

title: Quadratic Programming for Continuous Control of Safety-Critical Multiagent Systems Under Uncertainty
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control
evidence: Sec. III-IV: the QP takes the primary velocity command v_i^c and outputs a reference v_i^* as close as possible to it subject to barrier collision constraints (Eq. 25, 35-36), with a fallback v_i^*=0 once the relaxation variable hits zero (Eq. 41); Theorem 1 guarantees min inter-agent/obstacle distance >= D.
method: Feasible-set-reshaped, relaxed CBF-QP velocity filter for agents with uncertain IOS actuation dynamics; nonlinear small-gain analysis gives guaranteed multi-agent collision avoidance and Lipschitz control.
evaluation: Numerical examples (1-2 agents, 2 obstacles) comparing extended-margin, relaxed and reshaped QP on feasibility, |v*| continuity, min distance; three-quadrotor 2D physical experiment (Sec. VI). No timing reported in readable text.
contribution: Reshapes the feasible set of a collision-avoidance QP so a runtime velocity safety filter stays feasible, Lipschitz and provably safe for multiple agents with uncertain actuation dynamics.
flag: Section VI (simulations + three-quadrotor experiment) could not be read: arXiv HTML/PDF and ar5iv text all truncate in Sec. V; experiment details inferred from the authors' code repo (original vs reshaped QP, min-distance plots). Maintainer should confirm the quantitative baseline. Multi-agent hazard is pairwise collision only.

title: Risk-Aware Safe Control for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems via Dynamic Responsibility Allocation
venue: 2023 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. III-C, Eq. 7: each agent solves min ||u_i - u_bar_i||^2 s.t. A_i u_i <= omega_i b_i, minimally modifying the nominal control from a higher-level planner, with responsibility share omega_i = R_j/(R_i+R_j) recomputed every timestep from a CVaR-based CBF risk measure (Alg. 1).
method: Decentralized CBF-QP safety filter whose pairwise responsibility shares are allocated at runtime from a CVaR-based aggregate collision-risk measure under Gaussian motion uncertainty, without communication.
evaluation: Simulation only: 3-vehicle ramp merge (50 trials, distance >= 5 m, no baseline); 6-agent position swap vs centralized CBF and equal-share decentralized CBF on control deviation (44% shorter) and task time (402 vs 617 s).
contribution: Allocates collision-avoidance responsibility between agents at runtime from a CVaR risk measure, letting a decentralized CBF safety filter intervene less while keeping multi-agent interactions safe.
flag: Borderline E2: safety metric (min distance >= R_safe) reported without baseline; baselines are compared only on deviation/efficiency; number of trials for swap example not stated; no hardware or timing. Paper notes QP can be infeasible under input bounds.

title: Robust MADER: Decentralized and Asynchronous Multiagent Trajectory Planner Robust to Communication Delay
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. II-B, Alg. 1-2: during the Delay Check the agent keeps flying its committed trajectory and repeatedly tests the newly optimized trajectory against all received trajectories for delta_DC seconds; on conflict it discards the new trajectory and recommits the previous one, guaranteeing a collision-free trajectory when delta_DC >= delta_max.
method: Decentralized asynchronous multi-UAV trajectory planner that broadcasts both committed and candidate trajectories and gates commitment behind a delay-check window sized to worst-case communication delay.
evaluation: 100 sim runs, 10 UAVs, delays 0-300 ms vs MADER, EGO-Swarm, slow EGO-Swarm: collision rate (0% when delta_DC >= delta_max), stops, smoothness, travel time; 6-UAV hardware, 5 flights each: 0 vs 7 potential collisions; onboard planning, ~39 ms avg solve.
contribution: Makes decentralized asynchronous multi-UAV trajectory planning collision-free under communication delay by deferring commitment through a delay-check gate that rejects conflicting trajectories before execution.
flag: (d) is about communication delay bounds (delta_DC >= delta_max), not inference latency; maintainer may read it as (a)+(c) only. Safety cost is longer travel time and less smooth paths (reported). Hardware uses motion-capture localization.

title: Safe Adaptive Multi-Agent Coverage Control
venue: IEEE Control Systems Letters
evidence: Sec. III-B, Eq. 38: the control input minimizes ||u_i - u_hat_i||^2 against the nominal CVT coverage input subject to an adaptive barrier condition with h_i = ||p_i - z_i||^2 - (2 r_safe)^2 to the nearest neighbor; Theorem 1 proves safety under actuator faults and FAT-approximated disturbances.
method: Adaptive CBF-QP safety filter over a centroidal-Voronoi coverage controller, with projection-based estimation of actuator-effectiveness faults and Fourier function approximation of time-varying disturbances.
evaluation: Simulation only, 8 agents, 30 s, r_safe 0.25 m, theta=1/2: nominal CVT controller (no CBF) vs proposed; minimum pairwise distance over time (stays >= 2 r_safe) and paths. Single run, no coverage cost, no timing or hardware.
contribution: Adds an adaptive control-barrier safety filter to Voronoi coverage control so multi-agent area coverage remains collision-free despite actuator faults and unknown time-varying disturbances.
flag: Borderline E2: evaluation is one simulation with a min-distance plot against the no-CBF nominal controller; no statistics, no ablation of adaptive terms, experiments deferred to future work. Multi-agent hazard is pairwise collision only.

title: Safety-Critical Coordination for Cooperative Legged Locomotion via Control Barrier Functions
venue: 2023 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. III-A, Eq. 17: the top-level safety-critical planner solves a QP that minimally modifies a nominal desired velocity so that obstacle, coordination and holonomic-constraint CBFs hold on a reduced-order double-integrator model; the MPC and low-level layers then track the safe velocities.
method: Three-layer architecture for two rigidly connected quadrupeds: CBF-QP safe velocity planner, interconnected single-rigid-body MPC for ground reaction forces, distributed whole-body QP controllers.
evaluation: Reduced-order sim (2-4 obstacles, QP 0.9-1.3 ms via qpSWIFT), RaiSim full-order sim, two Unitree A1 hardware runs (2-3 obstacles); planner/MPC at 200 Hz, low-level 1 kHz. Only CBF-value and distance plots; no baseline, no ablation, no violation statistics.
contribution: Coordinates two physically coupled quadrupedal robots through a CBF-based safe planner layered over interconnected rigid-body MPC and distributed whole-body control, demonstrated on hardware.
flag: Qualitative demonstration only (plots show CBF values stay positive); no baseline or ablation. Multi-agent only nominally (two robots rigidly joined behave as one constrained body). Sub-ms QP solve times reported but no safety-metric comparison.

title: Spatial-Temporal-Aware Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Connected Autonomous Vehicles in Challenging Scenarios
venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV-B, Alg. 2: for each candidate action a nominal controller and CBF-QP check whether a safe input exists; only feasible actions enter the safe action set from which the policy samples (Alg. 1), and the agent falls back to an emergency stop if no action is feasible.
method: Constrained multi-agent A2C with GCN-Transformer spatial-temporal encoder over shared V2V observations, plus a parallel CBF-based Safety Shield that masks unsafe discrete actions before execution.
evaluation: CARLA: intersection and highway with hazard vehicles (3 CAVs), test-only Highway-Hard (5 CAVs, 10 vehicles); ablations w/o shield, FC encoder, w/o communication; collision-free rate 94/78% vs 20/0% without shield; Ryzen 3970X + 4 RTX 6000; no inference time.
contribution: Combines constrained multi-agent RL over a spatial-temporal graph encoder with a CBF-based action-masking safety shield, cutting collisions of connected vehicles facing unconnected hazard vehicles in CARLA.
flag: Shield masks actions rather than correcting them; paper does not state explicitly that the shield is active at test time (w/o-SS baseline implies it is). MAPPO/MACPO not compared. Encoder is representation learning, not a predictive world model, so (b) not credited.

title: Velocity Obstacle for Polytopic Collision Avoidance for Distributed Multi-Robot Systems
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
evidence: Sec. IV-D: metrics are completion rate, deadlock rate and average travel distance of polytopic VO/RVO/HRVO against circular-shaped variants; collision rate is not reported and Algorithm 1 only stops a robot after the polytope distance reaches zero.
method: Optimization-free velocity obstacles built from polytope vertex angles; each robot picks the velocity outside the combined VO closest to its preferred velocity; RVO/HRVO variants.
evaluation: Python simulation, 5-8 (video: 16) non-holonomic polytopic robots, 100 random trials; baselines circular VO/RVO/HRVO; completion, deadlock, travel distance; no compute-time numbers; laptop.
contribution: Vertex-based polytopic velocity obstacles for distributed multi-robot navigation, improving completion and deadlock rates over circular-approximation VO variants in randomized simulations.
flag: Navigation planner: collision avoidance is the design goal but measured outcomes are completion/deadlock/path length, not collision or hazard rate (primacy test fails); 'real-time' claim is qualitative only.

title: A Barrier-Based Scenario Approach to Verifying Safety-Critical Systems
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
evidence: Sec. IV-A/B: candidate barrier h is minimum pairwise inter-robot distance minus safe radius for 3-4 Robotarium robots; the randomized LP returns a probabilistic safety bound (gamma>=0) or a counterexample transition (one of 100 hardware trials showed h<0).
method: Offline scenario-based verification: sample initial conditions/parameters, record trajectories, solve randomized LP over barrier decay rate to get probabilistic safety guarantee or counterexample.
evaluation: Robotarium sim and hardware (3-4 robots), Unitree A1 quadruped with 4 static obstacles; metrics gamma*, violation bound epsilon vs empirical violation estimate (50 repeats); no baseline method; no LP solve times.
contribution: Randomized barrier-based scenario verification yielding probabilistic collision-safety guarantees or counterexamples for multi-robot systems from sampled trajectories, demonstrated on Robotarium hardware and a quadruped.
flag: Borderline: (c) plausibly met (multi-robot collision safety is the certified property, counterexample found on hardware) but there is no baseline or ablation, only bound-vs-empirical validation; entirely offline, no runtime element. Quadruped case is single-agent despite the abstract's 'multi-agent' wording.

title: AdverSAR: Adversarial Search and Rescue via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
venue: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Technologies for Homeland Security (HST)
evidence: Sec. V-A/Table IV: the only metric is mean flow-time (timesteps to find targets) in a 20x20 grid world; no collision or safety metrics are reported and robustness to the adversary comes only from alternating adversarial training (Algorithm 1).
method: Adversarial MARL (CTDE, hierarchical meta-learning) training cooperative SAR robots alongside a trained adversary that falsifies target locations; modified rewards.
evaluation: 20x20 grid world, 2 cooperative + 1 adversarial agent, 2 test maps; baseline target-conditioned rewards (Case III) and no-adversary cases; metric mean flow-time; no hardware/compute reported.
contribution: Adversarial multi-agent RL for search-and-rescue teams that remain effective when a teammate is replaced by an adversary spoofing target information, evaluated by flow-time in grid worlds.
flag: Adversarial teammate is a multi-agent hazard theme, but no safety outcome is measured and no runtime mechanism exists; training-time robustness only. Abstract claims partial communication but Sec. II states no explicit communication.

title: Data-Driven Robust Barrier Functions for Safe, Long-Term Operation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
evidence: Sec. V-VI: a QP minimally modifies the nominal control u_nom subject to robust CBF constraints A(x)u>=b(x) and actuator limits; Sec. VII-B/Table II: over 30 min with seven robots the robust filter had zero inter-robot constraint violations while the non-robust CBF baseline violated (first after 5 repetitions), QP at mean 220 Hz.
method: Robust control barrier functions for control-affine systems with disturbances modelled as unions of convex hulls (interval matrices), online GP disturbance learning, QP safety filter on nominal commands.
evaluation: Robotarium hardware, 7 GRITSBot-X robots, 30-min swap task; baseline non-robust CBF; metrics constraint violations (0 vs >0), throughput (42 vs 82 maneuvers), control deviation; QP mean 220 Hz.
contribution: Data-driven robust control barrier functions with online Gaussian-process disturbance learning act as a runtime QP safety filter, eliminating inter-robot collisions over 30 minutes of seven-robot hardware operation at the cost of throughput.
flag: Strong RQ5 datapoint: safety vs throughput trade-off (42 vs 82 maneuvers) and 56% higher control deviation; states 100 Hz real-time requirement and reports 220 Hz, but no edge hardware. Minor inconsistencies in constraint counts (2^m vs 2^2m) and experiment labelling.

title: Distributed Motion Coordination for Multirobot Systems Under LTL Specifications
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
evidence: Sec. IV-E, Algorithm 6 lines 14-16: if no feasible local trajectory is found within N_max iterations the robot enters Emerg mode and applies the braking controller until stopped; Theorem 1 guarantees no collisions if sensing radius exceeds twice the braking distance plus detection-period travel.
method: Three-layer distributed coordination: offline braking areas and transition systems, online conflict detection among neighbours with dynamic planning order, sampling-based local trajectory generation under LTL constraints, emergency braking fallback.
evaluation: MATLAB simulation only (i7 laptop), 4 unicycle robots with 3 obstacles, 2-16 double-integrator robots; no baselines or ablations; collision-freeness shown qualitatively by plots; replanning 1.51 s mean (3.30 s max), conflict detection every 0.1 s.
contribution: Fully distributed online motion coordination for LTL-tasked multi-robot teams with braking-area-based conflict detection, priority ordering and an emergency-braking fallback, with a formal collision-freedom guarantee.
flag: Emergency-brake fallback is a genuine execution-time halt (hence runtime_interceptor yes) and braking time is a time-to-irreversibility notion, but the paper is primarily a coordination/LTL planner (primacy test fails for c) and reports no quantitative collision metric or baseline; replanning latency 1.5-3.3 s is far from real-time.

title: Finite-time Motion Planning of Multi-agent Systems with Collision Avoidance
venue: 2022 13th Asian Control Conference (ASCC)
evidence: Sec. III: the controller (Eq. 5) is the gradient of a Lyapunov barrier function coupling goal distance and neighbour distance; Sec. IV reports only MATLAB plots of inter-agent distances for 4 and 20 single-integrator agents with no baselines, collision counts or convergence times.
method: Distributed finite-time controller derived from a Lyapunov barrier function for single-integrator agents, intended to give finite-time convergence to goals without inter-agent collisions.
evaluation: MATLAB numerical simulation only, 4 and 20 disk agents in a circular workspace; no baselines or ablations; qualitative distance plots; no compute time or hardware.
contribution: A Lyapunov-barrier-function distributed controller claimed to give finite-time multi-agent goal convergence with collision avoidance, shown only in numerical simulation.
flag: No quantitative safety metric or baseline; collision-avoidance part of Theorem 1 is not separately proved and the barrier does not diverge at the collision boundary; controller divides by a term that can be zero. Also E1-adjacent (controller design, not runtime safety).

title: Learning Enabled Fast Planning and Control in Dynamic Environments with Intermittent Information
venue: 2022 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. IV-A: the learned-reachability potential-field control iteration averaged 27 ms (max 81 ms) whereas computing one 600 s reachable set with Flow* took 67 s on average; the robot plans with information up to 9 minutes old and the reachability horizon T is chosen to cover the interval until the next data batch.
method: Neural networks trained offline on reachability-analysis (Flow*) repulsive fields approximate per-obstacle reachable-set potentials; online control sums attractive gradient and NN outputs for each non-cooperative obstacle.
evaluation: ROS Gazebo UUV crossing a shipping channel (20 trials; baselines direct reachability and no-uncertainty; min distance 7.5 m vs 18.8 m vs 1 collision), Jackal UGV with 2 TurtleBot obstacles via Vicon; 27 ms/81 ms per iteration.
contribution: Learned approximations of reachability-based repulsive fields let a robot with only stale, intermittent information about non-cooperative moving obstacles compute safe controls in tens of milliseconds instead of minutes.
flag: Borderline: single controlled robot avoiding non-cooperative agents (not multi-agent safety per se) and no runtime check/override, so (a) and (c) fail; included on (d) since fast inference of a safety-relevant predictive quantity is the primary claim with measured latency. Hardware experiments are single-trial without baselines; no edge hardware specified.

title: Learning Observation-Based Certifiable Safe Policy for Decentralized Multi-Robot Navigation
venue: 2022 International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV.A Policy Refinement: a CBF optimizer takes the RL action pi(s) as start value and solves a constrained problem for a nearby action; Algorithm 1 applies the refined action a* instead of the policy action; a deep transition model (Sec. III.B) predicts the next obstacle map and velocity.
method: Observation-based CBF optimizer refines RL policy actions at execution time using a learned one-step transition model; joint training feeds CBF Lagrangian back as reward.
evaluation: Sim: 4 and 8 robots (sparse/dense/empty), 20 rounds; baselines FDMCA, MNDS plus ablations (RL only, refine only); success, collision rate (0% vs 2.5-76%), time; real robots qualitative; no timing.
contribution: Observation-based CBF optimizer with a learned transition model refines RL actions at runtime, eliminating collisions in decentralized multi-robot navigation versus model-free RL baselines.
flag: CBF constraints are soft (relaxation variable, augmented Lagrangian) so not a hard veto; 'real-time' claimed with no measured latency; real-world results are trajectory images only; (b) is a pixel-level obstacle-map predictor rather than a graph/latent model.

title: MADER: Trajectory Planner in Multiagent and Dynamic Environments
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
evidence: Sec. V-A/V-D: collision avoidance is a constraint in the nonconvex trajectory optimization via separating planes; Sec. VI Check-Recheck tests a new plan against trajectories committed by others before commitment and otherwise 'keep[s] executing the trajectory found in the previous iteration'.
method: Decentralized asynchronous UAV trajectory planner (MINVO basis, separating planes as decision variables) with pre-commit Check-Recheck of shared committed trajectories.
evaluation: Sim only (desktop/laptop/cloud): corridor with 50-250 dynamic obstacles vs Bernstein/B-Spline; 4-32 agents vs SCP, RBP, DMPC, dec_iSCP; flight time, stops, distance, safety ratio; replan ~200 ms, check ~2.9 ms.
contribution: MADER plans asynchronous decentralized UAV trajectories around dynamic obstacles and other agents, reporting faster flights with fewer stops than Bernstein and B-Spline baselines in simulation.
flag: Planner where collision avoidance is one constraint; primary outcomes are flight time, stops and distance (primacy test fails). Borderline: Check-Recheck is a pre-commit veto of a new plan with explicit replan time budget delta_t, not an execution-time override; no hardware.

title: Nearest-Neighbor-based Collision Avoidance for Quadrotors via Reinforcement Learning
venue: 2022 International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. III Model (C): collision avoidance is learned only through a penalty c_c when another agent is within the avoidance radius; 'Actions are clipped after sampling to fulfill constraints' refers to velocity limits, no runtime shield is described.
method: Decentralized PPO policy with shared parameters observing only the single nearest neighbour; collision avoidance learned via reward; sim-to-real on Crazyflie quadrotors.
evaluation: Unity sim: 4-50 drones vs ORCA and FMP; packages collected, extra time to goal, min inter-agent distance; no collision rates; real Crazyflies 2-6 drones qualitative; on-board inference below 1 ms.
contribution: Nearest-neighbour-only observation lets a shared RL policy learn scalable decentralized quadrotor collision avoidance that transfers to real Crazyflies with sub-millisecond on-board inference.
flag: Borderline (c): collision avoidance is the primary claim but measured outcomes are task throughput and min inter-agent distance, with no collision/violation rate; no safety mechanism beyond the learned policy. On-board sub-1 ms inference on a microcontroller is relevant background for RQ1.

title: Resilient Monitoring in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems Through Network Reconfiguration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
evidence: Sec. V-C Algorithm 1 Comm_graph_gen: after a tolerable resource failure the base station adds communication edges via an MISDP until one-hop observability is restored, and an FCBF controller (Sec. VI) drives robots to realise the new links; no collision avoidance or action override is described.
method: Network reconfiguration after sensor-resource failures in heterogeneous robot teams using one-hop observability and finite-time-convergence CBF controllers to realise new communication edges.
evaluation: Nine Robotarium robots tracking five Crazyflies, six sequential faults; 20 random fault sequences vs random and greedy edge addition; metric tolerated faults and estimation error; no timing.
contribution: A one-hop observability criterion and FCBF-driven network reconfiguration keep heterogeneous robot teams monitoring an external process after sensor failures, outperforming random and greedy edge selection.
flag: Resilience/observability maintenance, not safety interception or hazard detection; fault detection assumed from existing methods; collision avoidance not mentioned; several internal inconsistencies between Table I and figure captions.

title: Responsibility-associated Multi-agent Collision Avoidance with Social Preferences
venue: 2022 IEEE 25th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC)
evidence: Sec. IV-B: at each timestep agent i solves a QP minimising ||u_i - u_bar_i||^2 subject to input bounds and the responsibility-weighted pairwise CBF constraint, where u_bar_i is 'assumed to be computed by a higher-level task-related planner'.
method: Decentralized CBF-QP safety filter with pairwise responsibility weights derived from Social Value Orientation, minimally modifying a nominal planner input for multi-agent collision avoidance.
evaluation: Matlab sim: 2-agent position swap and highway merge (trajectory plots only); 6-agent circular swap vs symmetric CBF; deadlock time, completion time, min distance; no collision counts, no hardware or timing.
contribution: Responsibility-associated SVO weights split pairwise CBF collision-avoidance constraints between heterogeneous agents, resolving deadlocks 46.8% faster than symmetric CBFs while remaining collision-free.
flag: Mechanism meets (a) and (c) but evaluation is largely qualitative: single runs, both baseline and method collision-free, outcome metric is deadlock/completion time rather than a hazard rate; maintainer may judge min-distance over 5 random theta sets as meeting the floor.

title: Safe Drone Flight with Time-Varying Backup Controllers
venue: 2022 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. II.C: the pilot's desired input is blended as rho = lambda*u_des + (1-lambda)*pi(x) with lambda = 1 - exp(-beta*max{0,h_I}), so the backup controller takes over at the boundary of the implicit safe set; Sec. III.D extends this to decentralized filtering of multiple drones.
method: Time-varying backup controllers define implicit CBFs; a runtime blending filter overrides pilot inputs as the backup-reachable set boundary nears, with online offset selection and maneuver switching; decentralized multi-drone extension.
evaluation: Two Cinewhoop drones with Teensy 4.1 at 100 Hz, OptiTrack 20 Hz; single-agent evade and two-drone head-on; baseline nominal backup controller in simulation only; qualitative plots, no violation counts or timing.
contribution: Time-varying backup controllers reduce the conservatism of backup-set safety filters, letting a runtime filter on a microcontroller safely override pilot inputs and deconflict two quadrotors.
flag: Runtime filter on edge hardware (100 Hz on Teensy) with human pilot input, but all results are qualitative: no quantitative safety metric, hardware baseline absent, pilot results simulated with scripted inputs. Human element is automation overriding a person, not deferral to a person, so (e) not credited.

title: Trust-based Rate-Tunable Control Barrier Functions for Non-Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems
venue: 2022 IEEE 61st Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
evidence: Algorithm 1: a CLF-QP computes a reference input u^r and a CBF-QP (Eq. 14) then minimally modifies it subject to barrier constraints for each neighbour, with the barrier rate alpha adapted online from a behaviour-based trust score (Sec. IV-B).
method: Rate-tunable CBF-QP safety filter whose class-K rate alpha is driven by an online trust metric estimated from each neighbour's observed constraint margin and heading relative to nominal.
evaluation: Single simulation: 3 intact unicycles, 1 adversarial and 2 uncooperative agents; baseline fixed-alpha CBF described as failing to reach goals; qualitative trust/alpha/barrier plots only; no numbers, hardware or timing.
contribution: Trust estimated from observed behaviour tunes the rate of control barrier functions so cooperative agents stay safe yet less conservative among non-cooperative and adversarial agents.
flag: Runtime CBF filter in a non-cooperative multi-agent setting, but evaluation is one qualitative scenario with no tabulated safety or conservatism metrics; authors note the trust function is not Lipschitz and inputs are unbounded.

title: AgentLeak: A Benchmark for Internal-Channel Privacy Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
venue: IEEE Access
evidence: Sec. VI Defense Interceptor Experiment: a prototype interceptor 'masked vault fields outside the channel-specific allowed set and blocked raw vault transmission in inter-agent messages and memory writes', cutting internal leakage from 31.5% to 2.4%.
method: Benchmark of 7 internal communication channels in coordinator-worker LLM systems; LLM-judge leak detection on captured traces; prototype runtime interceptor masking/blocking vault fields in inter-agent messages.
evaluation: 1,000 scenarios (healthcare/finance/legal/corporate), 5 production LLMs; single- vs multi-agent baseline; defenses incl. LlamaGuard; metrics ELR/CLR/ASR/TSR; CPU-only; no latency figures.
contribution: Shows multi-agent LLM systems leak less in final output (27.2% vs 43.2%) but 68.9% across internal channels, and a runtime inter-agent interceptor cuts internal leakage to 2.4% at a 4.7-point task-success cost.
flag: Privacy/security hazard rather than physical safety; interceptor is a side experiment on 120 scenarios, main contribution is the benchmark; interceptor latency not reported; multi-agent = two agents only.

title: LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Control for Skill-Based Smart Manufacturing
venue: 2026 IEEE 31st International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
evidence: Sec. IV-C/V-B: the only safeguard is a ToolAvailabilityManager that filters each agent's tool list before the LLM call so operations 'that would be rejected by the underlying controllers' are not offered; no validator inspects or blocks executed actions, and fault recovery is attributed to LLM reasoning (Sec. IV-C).
method: One LLM agent per factory module via MCP tool servers over OPC UA, MQTT coordination and live state injection; orchestrator, peer-to-peer and monolithic architectures compared.
evaluation: Simulated six-module hexagonal factory, 9 challenges x 10 runs, Gemma4:31B on RTX 6000 Pro; architecture comparison plus one state-injection ablation; solve rate 87-93%, wall-clock 163-353 s per production.
contribution: Compares orchestrator, peer-to-peer and monolithic LLM multi-agent architectures for skill-based manufacturing control, finding only the orchestrator reroutes around a silent conveyor fault in every run.
flag: Multi-agent coordination/programming, not a safety mechanism; primary outcome is task solve rate; operator refill confirmation (Challenge 4) is the only human element; human review before deployment is future work.

title: Logic-Based Verification of Task Allocation for LLM-Enabled Multi-Agent Manufacturing Systems
venue: 2026 18th International Workshop on Discrete Event Systems (WODES)
evidence: Sec. IV/Fig. 3: the Central Controller Agent compiles the LLM-generated task allocation into a DES automaton and checks it against LTLf safety automata by reachability 'before execution'; violations are fed back with a witness trace for replanning (Sec. IV-C), raising rule satisfaction from 50-76% (pure LLM) to 86-93% (Table II).
method: LLM product agents plan multi-robot task DAGs; central controller composes plan automaton with LTLf-derived safety automata and DFS-checks violation reachability before execution, returning counterexamples for bounded replanning.
evaluation: Three multi-robot assembly scenarios (2-4 robots, 2-4 rules), GPT-5, 20 trials; baseline pure LLM with NL constraints; rule satisfaction 92.5/91.7/86.3% vs 50/75.9/50%; verification 0.10-25.5 s; hardware unspecified.
contribution: Verifies LLM-generated multi-robot task allocations against LTLf safety rules via DES reachability before execution, lifting safety-rule satisfaction from 50-76% to 86-93% over a prompt-only LLM baseline.
flag: Gate operates at plan level before execution of each plan, not during execution; authors list online runtime verification as future work; verification time grows to 25 s at 4 robots; simulated vs physical setup not stated; 8-14% of rules still violated after repair.

title: The Trust Paradox in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: When Collaboration Becomes a Security Vulnerability
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
evidence: Sec. III-V: closed-loop two-agent exchanges at trust levels 0.1/0.5/0.9 are scored against a Minimum-Necessary-Information baseline; Over-Exposure Rate rises on average +0.26 from low to high trust, and Sensitive-Information Repartitioning and a Guardian Agent reduce Authorization Drift by 38-88% (Sec. V-E).
method: Formalises Trust-Vulnerability Paradox; custodian/seeker LLM dyad with explicit trust parameter; metrics OER and AD vs MNI baseline; defenses: k-of-n information repartitioning and a prompt-based Guardian Agent with pre-speak MNI-Gate.
evaluation: 19 sub-scenes, 1,488 chains, AgentScope/AutoGen/LangGraph, GPT/DeepSeek/Qwen/Llama-3-8B; MNI baseline; OER at tau=0.9 cut 20-49% by defenses; no hardware/latency figures, overhead described only as 'moderate'.
contribution: Shows that raising inter-agent trust in LLM multi-agent systems increases over-exposure of sensitive data, and that information repartitioning or a guardian agent cuts authorization drift by 38-88%.
flag: Borderline (c): security/privacy over-exposure rather than physical hazard; whether MNI-Gate/Guardian Agent is a code-level runtime interceptor or prompt-only is not stated; defense task-success numbers not reported; no human in loop.

title: UAVBench: An Open Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous and Agentic AI UAV Systems via LLM-Generated Flight Scenarios
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology
evidence: Sec. III-C/IV: safety checks (separation, time-to-collision, geofence) are applied by Algorithm 1 only when validating generated JSON scenarios for the dataset; evaluation is 32 LLMs answering multiple-choice questions, with 'dynamic simulation rollouts' left as future work (Sec. V).
method: Taxonomy-guided LLM generation of 50k UAV flight scenarios with schema/constraint/geometry/safety validation and risk labels, plus 50k MCQs across ten reasoning styles.
evaluation: Offline MCQ accuracy of 32 LLMs (e.g. Qwen3 235B 83.5%, GPT-5 80.2%); no acting system, no baseline or ablation, no hardware, cost or latency; multi-agent coordination items below 80%.
contribution: Releases UAVBench, 50k validated LLM-generated UAV flight scenarios with risk labels and a 50k-question reasoning benchmark evaluated on 32 LLMs.
flag: Dataset/benchmark only; no runtime mechanism, no acting agent, no baseline (also fails E2); multi-agent only as scenario content; companion to alpha3-Bench (2601.03281) in same batch.

title: α3-Bench: A Unified Benchmark of Safety, Robustness, and Efficiency for LLM-Based UAV Agents Over 6G Networks
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems
evidence: Sec. III-C.3(b), Eq. 32: Safety Policy is scored post hoc per episode (penalties 0.25-0.50 for altitude, no-fly-zone, separation and battery violations); Sec. III-A.4 calls the policy layer a 'supervisory constraint' but no blocking mechanism is implemented, and the only runtime stop is episode termination on violation (Sec. III-B.8).
method: Multi-turn benchmark of LLM UAV agents with simulated human operator, MCP tool calls and A2A peer coordination under simulated 6G slices (latency, jitter, loss, edge load); six-pillar composite score.
evaluation: 113k episodes, 17 LLMs, deterministic decoding; models compared only to each other (no baseline/ablation); Safety Policy 0.88-1.00, Network Robustness 0.785-0.937; API wall-clock only, no hardware.
contribution: Benchmarks 17 LLM UAV agents on mission outcome, safety compliance, tool consistency and robustness under simulated 6G latency, jitter and loss, finding robustness drops sharply when the network degrades.
flag: Borderline (c): safety is one of six scored pillars, post hoc, with no baseline or ablation; latency/jitter are simulated inputs to the agent, not inference-latency constraints; human operator is scripted/LLM-simulated, no handoff; abstract and tables disagree on several figures.

title: A Multi-Agent LLM Defense Pipeline Against Prompt Injection Attacks
venue: 2025 IEEE International Women in Engineering (WIE) Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (WIECON-ECE)
evidence: Sec. III.B.2/Fig. 2: the Coordinator classifies each incoming query before the Domain LLM is invoked and flagged inputs 'receive a predefined safe refusal'; Sec. III.B.1: the Guard checks each candidate answer for policy violations before release; ASR falls from 20-30% to 0% (Table VI).
method: Pipeline of specialised LLM agents (Coordinator pre-input classifier with policy store; Domain LLM; post-generation Guard) in sequential and hierarchical configurations to block prompt-injection attacks.
evaluation: 55 attacks in 8 categories, ~400 evaluations on ChatGLM-6B and Llama2-13B; baselines undefended forwarding and rule-based filter; Guard off/on ablation; ASR 20-30% to 0%; no false-positive rate, hardware or latency.
contribution: A coordinator-plus-guard pipeline of specialised LLM agents intercepts prompt-injection inputs and outputs for a single chatbot, reducing attack success from 20-30% to 0% on 55 attacks.
flag: Single-agent, single-input guardrail: 'multi-agent' refers to the defense components, protected system is one QA chatbot; claims 'real-time' without latency data; no false-positive or utility numbers; attack counts inconsistent across tables (380 vs 400).

title: Assessing and Enhancing the Robustness of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems Through Chaos Engineering
venue: 2025 IEEE/ACM 4th International Conference on AI Engineering – Software Engineering for AI (CAIN)
evidence: Sec. I/III: proposes a chaos-engineering framework that 'simulates agent failures, communication delays, and other disruptions in controlled settings' for LLM-MAS; Sec. V only plans metrics (response time, fault detection rate, error rate) with no results.
method: PhD research proposal: chaos-engineering loop (chaos modelling, fault injection, evaluation) to probe LLM multi-agent system robustness; literature review and GitHub analysis only.
evaluation: No experiments; planned metrics (response time, fault detection/error rates, CPU/memory) and planned comparison with existing robustness methods; case studies with Deloitte proposed; no hardware or numbers.
contribution: Proposal for a chaos-engineering framework to inject agent failures, communication delays and cascading faults into LLM multi-agent systems to assess and improve robustness.
flag: Research proposal with no evaluation; cascading-failure scenarios are only named, not studied; nothing to extract. Multi-agent only nominally so far.

title: Hidden in Plain Text: Measuring LLM Deception Quality Against Human Baselines Using Social Deduction Games
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Agentic AI (ICA)
evidence: Sec. III.C/IV: a GPT-4-Turbo 'Mafia Detector' reads role-redacted transcripts; 'We use prediction accuracy as a surrogate marker for deception quality' (Abstract); single-match accuracy 52.27% on LLM games vs 58.62% on human games vs ~38-40% random.
method: Asynchronous 10-agent GPT-4o Mafia games; post-hoc GPT-4-Turbo detector predicts mafia from transcripts; detector accuracy used as proxy for LLM deception quality vs humans.
evaluation: 35 LLM games vs 28 human games; Monte Carlo random-guess baseline; single/exact-match detection accuracy (LLM 52.27%/8.09%, human 58.62%/12.64%); no hardware or latency reported.
contribution: Measures LLM deception quality in asynchronous multi-agent Mafia games by comparing a transcript-based mafia detector's accuracy on LLM versus human play.
flag: Borderline (c): multi-agent LLM safety-adjacent evaluation (deception) with a baseline, but no hazard mechanism or detection/interception method; post-hoc analysis only. Maintainer may consider as background for LLM-agent deception detection.

title: KoMA: Knowledge-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous Driving With Large Language Models
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles
evidence: Sec. III-C/Algorithm 1: plans are reviewed at planning time ('If the plan is deemed infeasible, it craft a new plan') and actions go straight to env.step(action); safety enters only as a TTC-based reflection score after the episode (Sec. III-E).
method: KoMA: LLM driving agents with multi-agent intention inference, multi-step planning, shared vector memory and ranking-based post-hoc reflection; safety via TTC scoring of past decisions, no runtime filter.
evaluation: highway-env on-ramp merge (2 LLM + 5 IDM vehicles), roundabout generalisation; vs MARL and DiLu; success rate 70% at 40 rounds vs MARL 65% at 40k; no collision rate, hardware or latency reported.
contribution: Knowledge-driven LLM multi-agent driving framework with shared memory and ranking-based reflection that improves merge success rate over MARL and DiLu baselines in highway-env.
flag: Planner/coordination paper; collision avoidance is one scored criterion among efficiency and success; no runtime interception; agents do not interact directly (Sec. III-B). Fails primacy test for (c).

title: PeerGuard: Defending Multi-Agent Systems Against Backdoor Attacks Through Mutual Reasoning
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Information Reuse and Integration and Data Science (IRI)
evidence: Sec. III-C: each agent must 'assess the consistency between the reasoning process and the final output' of its peers to flag a poisoned agent; Sec. IV-B.2: 'PeerGuard has a TPR range from 75% to 96%' vs Auto-CoT ~0.10-0.50 and ZS-CoT ~0.40-0.80, with clean-agent FPR mostly under 6% (Tables IV-VI).
method: PeerGuard: prompt-based mutual-reasoning defence in LLM multi-agent debate; agents check peers' reasoning-answer consistency to detect backdoored agents, no fine-tuning, API-only access.
evaluation: Two-agent debate (GPT-4o, Llama3-70B) on MMLU, CommonsenseQA, ARC; BadWord backdoor; vs ZS-CoT and Auto-CoT templates; TPR 0.75-0.97, FPR <6-10%; AutoGen/CAMEL check; no hardware or latency.
contribution: PeerGuard lets LLM agents in a multi-agent debate detect backdoored peers by checking reasoning-output consistency, reaching 75-96% detection with low false positives against prompting baselines.
flag: Detection runs at inference time but the paper defines no veto/block/halt action after flagging, so runtime_interceptor=no and (a) not met; (c) met as a multi-agent detector with TPR/FPR vs baselines. Baselines are reasoning templates, not established backdoor defences; text/table FPR figures inconsistent.

title: Position Paper: Emergent Machina Sapiens Urge Rethinking Multi-Agent Paradigms in Critical Infrastructures
venue: 2025 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
evidence: Sec. 3.2: 'Protocols can emerge as penalties on agents' objectives' (Eq. 1) and 'may act as constraints that limit the actions of agents'; Sec. 3.3: 'Evaluating such a framework requires metrics that capture...' with no experiments reported.
method: Position paper: argues for emergent, self-organising multi-agent AI in critical infrastructure with learnable norms/protocols as objective penalties; two illustrative case studies (vehicles, energy markets).
evaluation: No experiments, simulations, baselines or numbers; metrics (utility, fairness, norm stability, adaptability) proposed conceptually only; no hardware or latency.
contribution: Position paper arguing that multi-agent AI in critical infrastructure needs emergent, learnable norms rather than fixed game-theoretic rules, illustrated by vehicle and energy-market scenarios.
flag: Position paper with no evaluation (also arguably E3-like); cascading-failure example in Sec. 4.1 and call for real-time monitoring of emergent dynamics (Sec. 5.1) are future-work statements only. HTML rate-limited; read from PDF.

title: Can LLMs Understand Social Norms in Autonomous Driving Games?
venue: 2024 IEEE International Automated Vehicle Validation Conference (IAVVC)
evidence: Sec. II-A: 'the action choosing policy of an agent was solely decided by LLMs'; crash gives -5 reward and terminates the game; Sec. IV-A: yielding rate 0.96-1.0, crashes in 2/50 runs with no background vehicles; no baseline.
method: GPT-4 agents choose Go/Stop/lane-change in two grid Markov driving games (unsignalized intersection, highway platoon) to test emergence of yielding and platooning norms.
evaluation: Custom grid simulator, 50 runs per background-vehicle count (0-4); no baselines; metrics yielding rate 0.96-1.0, platoon rate 0.80-0.98, early stops; reward ablation (-2 to 0 Go reward); no hardware or latency.
contribution: Shows GPT-4 driving agents in grid Markov games spontaneously adopt yielding and platooning norms, with a reward ablation exposing a waiting-time versus crash trade-off.
flag: Primary claim and outcome is norm formation (yield/platoon rate), not hazard rate; crashes reported only incidentally; no runtime mechanism; no baseline. HTML rate-limited; read from PDF.

title: A Scalable Distributed Collision Avoidance Scheme for Multi-agent UAV systems
venue: 2021 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. I-B: 'the collision avoidance is solved for in the control layer' as NMPC constraints; Sec. II: lab tests with up to 10 Crazyflies, min inter-agent distance 0.33-0.38 m, avg solver time 1.46-5.35 ms under a 40 ms per-step cap at 20 Hz, 'there was no collisions with any agent' (Sec. II-B.3).
method: Distributed NMPC per UAV treating broadcast predicted trajectories of neighbours as moving spherical obstacles; proximity-ranked obstacle prioritisation keeps 3 constraints per agent; PANOC+ALM solver (OpEn, Rust).
evaluation: Lab experiments with up to 10 Crazyflie 2.0 UAVs (Vicon), one non-cooperative piloted UAV; no baselines or ablations; min distance 0.33-0.38 m, solver 1.46-5.35 ms, <1% hit 40 ms cap; off-board ThinkPad i7.
contribution: Scalable distributed NMPC collision avoidance for UAV swarms that ranks neighbours' broadcast trajectories to bound per-agent constraints, running at 20 Hz with millisecond solve times on up to ten drones.
flag: Collision avoidance is the primary claim and min-distance the primary outcome (c), with an explicit 40 ms solver deadline (d), but no baseline or ablation, so fails the v1.5 evaluation floor; (a) not met since avoidance is a planner constraint, not a runtime shield. Compute is off-board laptop, not edge. Possible RQ1 background.

title: Collision Avoidance in Pedestrian-Rich Environments With Deep Reinforcement Learning
venue: IEEE Access
evidence: Sec. IV-B: percent collisions is the primary metric vs ORCA, SA-CADRL and DRLMACA; for 6-10 agents the LSTM policy 'shows a 3-4x reduction in failed cases with similar' extra time to goal.
method: Decentralised deep-RL collision-avoidance policy (GA3C-CADRL); LSTM encodes arbitrary number of observed agents; safety only via collision/near-miss reward and episode termination.
evaluation: Simulation 2-40 agents, 500 random cases; baselines ORCA, SA-CADRL, DRLMACA; ablations (LSTM, ordering); % collisions, % stuck, extra time; policy query 0.4-0.5 ms CPU; qualitative multirotor and ground-robot demos.
contribution: Shows an LSTM-based deep-RL policy reduces collisions 3-4x among 6-10 non-communicating heterogeneous agents versus prior learned and ORCA planners, with sub-millisecond CPU inference.
flag: Borderline (c): a learned navigation policy, not a detector or interceptor, but collision rate vs baselines is the primary claim and outcome; no formal guarantee; hardware results qualitative only; v4 is the extended IEEE Access version of the IROS'18 GA3C-CADRL paper.

title: Congestion-aware Multi-agent Trajectory Prediction for Collision Avoidance
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. III: multi-agent trajectory prediction where a teacher learns latent congestion patterns (GMM) over an agent graph with collision-time edges and a student is matched to it via a KL upper bound; Table II reports collision rate of predicted trajectories vs V-LSTM, CS-LSTM, S-GAN.
method: Congestion-aware teacher-student trajectory predictor (CF-LSTM): teacher infers latent congestion patterns over an agent interaction graph; student matches that distribution via variational bound while predicting all agents' trajectories.
evaluation: Simulation only: synthetic GTA collision-avoidance dataset and NGSIM US-101; baselines V-LSTM, CS-LSTM, S-GAN, MFP etc.; collision rate (5.31% vs 5.53-7.51%) and RMSE; mixture-count ablation; no compute time reported.
contribution: Learns latent congestion patterns over a multi-agent interaction graph so a student predictor yields fewer predicted collisions than V-LSTM, CS-LSTM and S-GAN on synthetic and NGSIM highway data.
flag: Meets (b) only; no safety mechanism, prediction is offline-evaluated; collision-rate margins small (5.31% vs 5.53%) with no variance reported; evaluation floor met via baselines.

title: Human-Inspired Multi-Agent Navigation using Knowledge Distillation
venue: 2021 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. III-C: safety handled only by 'a negative reward signal r_collision as a penalty to those that collide with any other agent'; Table I metrics are success rate, extra distance and energy efficiency, no collision rate.
method: Decentralised multi-agent navigation RL with knowledge distillation: experts behaviour-cloned from human pedestrian data shape the reward to produce human-like collision-avoidance paths.
evaluation: Simulation only (6-20 agents, circle/corridor/crossing); baselines ORCA, SL expert, RL without distillation; ablations on experts/reward terms; success rate, extra distance, energy; training ~6 h on 2 V100s; no inference latency.
contribution: Combines RL with knowledge distillation from human-trajectory experts so decentralised agents navigate in a human-like way, outperforming ORCA and plain RL on success and efficiency metrics.
flag: Multi-agent coordination/human-likeness paper; collision avoidance is one constraint, no safety metric or runtime mechanism.

title: MAPS-X: Explainable Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Segmentation
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. III: MAPS-X 'only adds nodes that have a satisfiable number of explanations to graph (tree) G' during planning; the human role is offline verification of segment images, with no user study and no collision-rate metric (Table I: success rate, runtime, segment count).
method: Meta-algorithm wrapping centralised sampling-based multi-robot planners (RRT/EST) to bound the number of disjoint-trajectory segments so a plan is explainable as a few images.
evaluation: Simulation only (OMPL, 2-3 robots, four environments, 200 runs); comparison MAPS-RRT vs Lazy MAPS-RRT over bound r; success rate, runtime (seconds), segment count; AMD Ryzen 7; no collision metric.
contribution: Introduces MAPS-X, planners that trade computation for multi-robot plans explainable to a human supervisor as a short sequence of non-intersecting path-segment images.
flag: Planning-time explainability, not runtime handoff; human verification claimed but not measured; tangential background for RQ3 slow-explanation channel.

title: Meta Preference Learning for Fast User Adaptation in Human-Supervisory Multi-Robot Deployments
venue: 2021 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. IV-C: human instructions Ins in {+1,0,-1} update preference labels; Sec. V-B reports intervention duration '42.4% shorter than that of the baseline method'; no collision or safety-violation rate reported and no runtime filter described.
method: Meta Preference Learning: MAML/Reptile meta-learned neural preference model adapts flocking parameters (spacing, height, speed, safety distance) of a five-UAV team from a few human corrective instructions.
evaluation: AirSim/Unreal simulation only, 5 UAVs, ~20,000 simulated preferences from 20 users; baseline non-meta preference model; L2 loss, intervention duration and count; no safety metric, no compute time.
contribution: Meta-learns user preference models so a supervised multi-UAV search team adapts to a new operator from few corrections, cutting human intervention time by 42% in simulation.
flag: Human-supervisory adaptation, not takeover/handoff when automation defers; safety distance is a tunable preference, not a measured outcome; small samples, no significance tests.

title: Multi-UAV Path Planning for Wireless Data Harvesting With Deep Reinforcement Learning
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
evidence: Sec. III-B, Eq. 16: a rule-based safety controller rejects actions that enter buildings/NFZs, collide with an active UAV or land outside the landing zone; 'If rejected, the resulting safe action is the hovering action.'
method: Multi-UAV DDQN with global-local map inputs for IoT data harvesting (Dec-POMDP, centralised training/decentralised execution); rule-based runtime safety controller replaces unsafe actions with hover; soft penalties for flight-time violation.
evaluation: Grid-world simulation only (Manhattan32, Urban50), 1000 Monte Carlo runs; baseline scalar-input DQNs; landing success 99.4%/98.8%, collection ratio; no collision rate, no ablation of safety controller; FLOPs only, 40 h training on Titan Xp.
contribution: Trains a single map-based DDQN policy that generalises across fleet size and sensor layout for multi-UAV data harvesting, with a rule-based action filter enforcing no-fly and inter-UAV collision constraints.
flag: Runtime interceptor exists (action-replacement safety controller) but is incidental: paper's subject is data-harvesting throughput; safety controller not evaluated or ablated, no collision metric; flight-time safety is a soft learned penalty.

title: Prediction-Based Reachability for Collision Avoidance in Autonomous Driving
venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV-C, Eq. 7: the robot follows its original controller when both safety values are positive, otherwise switches to the car-safety or curb controller; Table I: Default 3/10 vs Reachability-Pred 0/0 close encounters (<=0.5 m/<=1 m) in intersection case 1.
method: HJ-reachability safety filter for two-car driving: human behaviour clustered into six driving modes, per-mode BRTs precomputed as lookup tables, online mode prediction selects a less conservative BRT that overrides the nominal controller when value <= 0.
evaluation: Simulation only (INTERACTION T-intersection and 8-way roundabout, 3 cases each, 10-20 trials); baselines no safety controller and reachability without prediction; close-encounter counts, path deviation, safety-controller activation time; prediction assumed perfect; no compute time measured.
contribution: Uses mode-conditioned HJ reachability so a runtime safety controller overrides nominal driving only when needed, keeping near-collisions near zero while reducing interventions and path deviation versus unconditioned reachability.
flag: Multi-agent only pairwise (two cars); prediction assumed 100% correct so the probabilistic guarantee is untested; 'real time' claimed via table lookup but no latency measured; Table I trial/time-step counting ambiguous.

title: Towards Safe Control of Continuum Manipulator Using Shielded Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
evidence: Sec. II-C: the shield is 'placed after MADQN'; Algorithm 1 applies shielding to the chosen actions before executing the shielded joint action; when tip error is below K=2 mm the action boundary is scaled to beta*|delta| (Algorithm 2).
method: Two-agent DQN (one agent per DoF) controls a 2-DoF cable-driven continuum surgical manipulator; a post-policy saturation shield clamps action step size near the target before execution.
evaluation: Physical robot + sim; ablation with/without shield on circle/square/infinity trajectories at 20 Hz: RMS error 0.68/0.54/0.71 mm -> 0.31/0.28/0.24 mm; vs KMOC baseline; payload, soft/rigid obstacle, Nitinol robot; no inference latency.
contribution: A post-policy saturation shield on a two-agent DQN controller halves tracking error of a cable-driven continuum surgical manipulator on hardware, with payloads and obstacle contact.
flag: Multi-agent only nominally: the two 'agents' are the two DoFs of one robot. Shield is a runtime action clamp (meets (a) formally) but targets overshoot/oscillation, not hazards; metrics are tracking error, no collision/violation rate.

title: V-RVO: Decentralized Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance using Voronoi Diagrams and Reciprocal Velocity Obstacles
venue: 2021 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. III-A/B: each agent plans toward a goal point on its braking-aware buffered Voronoi cell boundary outside the RVO cones; collision freedom (Theorem 1) holds only if all agents use V-RVO; no separate filter overrides a nominal command.
method: Decentralized multi-agent collision avoidance combining buffered Voronoi cells (shrunk by braking distance for double integrators) with RVO cones, plus a heuristic position-swap deadlock-resolution mode.
evaluation: Simulation only, 4-70 agents, circle swap/head-on/formation scenarios vs ORCA; results are trajectory plots, no collision counts or success rates; 1-2 ms per agent on 2.7 GHz i7 desktop.
contribution: V-RVO fuses braking-aware buffered Voronoi cells with reciprocal velocity obstacles for decentralized navigation of up to 70 agents, reported as less conservative than ORCA.
flag: Navigation planner: collision avoidance is embedded in the planner, paper is about conservativeness/deadlock vs ORCA; also fails E2 (qualitative plots only, no collision rate).

title: Barrier Functions for Multiagent-POMDPs with DTL Specifications
venue: 2020 59th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
evidence: Sec. IV: Algorithm 1 at every time step propagates the joint belief under the nominal joint action, tests the discrete-time barrier condition and, if it fails, replaces the action with a safe joint action that 'minimally changes the immediate reward from the nominal immediate reward'; the shield 'checks the satisfaction of the LDTL safety properties real-time at every time step'.
method: Minimally interfering runtime shield for multi-agent POMDPs: discrete-time barrier functions over the joint belief enforce linear distribution temporal logic (safety and finite-time reachability) on top of a nominal policy.
evaluation: Single ROS/Gazebo sim with 3 heterogeneous robots (drone, Flipper, Segway); nominal A*/constant policy vs shielded policy; metric is barrier-value trace (negative under nominal, positive with shield); no violation rates, hardware or compute time.
contribution: Discrete-time barrier functions over joint beliefs give a minimally interfering runtime shield that enforces temporal-logic safety specifications on a nominal policy for heterogeneous multi-robot POMDPs.
flag: Borderline on E2: closest conceptual fit in batch (true runtime shield over multi-agent belief, nominal policy may come from a human operator) but evaluation is one simulated run with barrier-value plots, no violation rate or repeated trials; maintainer may accept nominal-vs-shield trace as baseline.
